claims.assertion: The rider was charged a $6.61 cancellation fee ("no-show") after the driver cancelled, so the charge is only valid if every condition of NS-1 is met.
NS-1(i) fails: the driver never pressed "I'm Here" — the timeline field for that tap is null (F7) — so the first mandatory condition for the $6.61 fee is not satisfied.

The driver's written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes" (F12, repeated in chat F10-F11) is contradicted by the system timeline, and the chat/timeline conflict must be resolved in favour of the system record, which shows no arrival-button tap at all.
Because NS-1 is not satisfied on its own terms, NS-0 routes the dispute to NS-2: the $6.61 must be refunded in full to the rider.

The system timeline itself records the driver's "arrival" at 17:17:50 and cancellation only 4 min 40 s later, while the driver stayed parked from 17:18:25 to 17:22:30 — so the driver did have the opportunity to press "I'm Here" and chose not to, which is precisely the evidential gap NS-2 addresses.

The rider's own account (coming out about a minute after cancellation) is consistent with the GPS record that the driver was stationary only 53 m from the pickup point when he cancelled, so there was no genuine no-show to justify the fee.
No aggravating traffic or weather excuse exists that could explain the driver's conduct: no incidents were recorded near the route, no speed bands applied, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.

Independently of the refund, the driver's account is a candidate for review: he asserted in writing that he had pressed "I'm Here" when the timeline shows no such tap, and NS-2 provides for a flag_account referral where the arrival/cancellation flow is used without the required GPS/button conditions.

weaknesses: The rider will have to explain the profile record (F16): 3 disputes in 90 days with 2 no-show disputes upheld, which the driver side will use to argue the rider is a repeat late-canceller.

The GPS record is partly unhelpful to us: the driver was within 200 m from 17:17:50 and stayed within range for 4 min 40 s (F2, F3) — on a plain reading the rider was inside a 200 m radius of a waiting car and did not board, which the driver will use under NS-1(iii).

The driver's chat at 17:19 (F10) and 17:22 (F11) supports his version that he was waiting at the pickup and had waited over 3 minutes; the timeline's null arrival tap (F7) conflicts with the driver statement (F12) and is our case's narrowest point.
The driver's clean record (F17: 394 trips in 90 d, rating 4.4, 0 disputes) makes a fraud-style flag_account referral harder to sustain, and flag_account can only ever be an add-on, not the outcome.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.78)
events.body:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show case, so the $6.61 charge is valid only if NS-1 is satisfied; NS-0 routes the dispute accordingly [F4][F8][NS-0]. Every NS-1 element is present on the executed trace: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:18:50 [F6], he was 38 m from the pickup at the moment of the tap (closest approach 34 m) [F6][F1], and he remained inside the 200 m radius for 220 s after the tap until cancelling [F6][F2][F3], satisfying (i), (ii) and (iii) respectively [NS-1].

The rider's core argument is that F7's null driver_pressed_here_at field destroys NS-1(i) and pushes the case into NS-2 [F7][F12][NS-2]. The trace resolves the F6/F7 conflict in favour of the positive, time-stamped system entry F6 — a tap at 17:18:50 with a measured 38 m distance and a corresponding 220 s within-radius interval — which is also consistent with the driver's chat message at 17:19 [F10] and his statement [F12]; a bare null field in a second timeline fact is the weaker record and does not displace it [NS-1]. The rider's advocate effectively conceded (ii) and (iii) in rebuttal, leaving (i) as the only live element, and (i) is met [F6][NS-1].

what_would_change: Had the driver tapped I'm Here more than 200 m away, or left before 3 minutes, NS-2 would refund the fee in full.

claims.assertion: The rider was charged a $6.61 cancellation fee ("no-show") after the driver cancelled, so the charge is only valid if every condition of NS-1 is met.
NS-1(i) fails: the driver never pressed "I'm Here" — the timeline field for that tap is null (F7) — so the first mandatory condition for the $6.61 fee is not satisfied.

The driver's written statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes" (F12, repeated in chat F10-F11) is contradicted by the system timeline, and the chat/timeline conflict must be resolved in favour of the system record, which shows no arrival-button tap at all.
Because NS-1 is not satisfied on its own terms, NS-0 routes the dispute to NS-2: the $6.61 must be refunded in full to the rider.

The system timeline itself records the driver's "arrival" at 17:17:50 and cancellation only 4 min 40 s later, while the driver stayed parked from 17:18:25 to 17:22:30 — so the driver did have the opportunity to press "I'm Here" and chose not to, which is precisely the evidential gap NS-2 addresses.

The rider's own account (coming out about a minute after cancellation) is consistent with the GPS record that the driver was stationary only 53 m from the pickup point when he cancelled, so there was no genuine no-show to justify the fee.
No aggravating traffic or weather excuse exists that could explain the driver's conduct: no incidents were recorded near the route, no speed bands applied, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain.

Independently of the refund, the driver's account is a candidate for review: he asserted in writing that he had pressed "I'm Here" when the timeline shows no such tap, and NS-2 provides for a flag_account referral where the arrival/cancellation flow is used without the required GPS/button conditions.

weaknesses: The rider will have to explain the profile record (F16): 3 disputes in 90 days with 2 no-show disputes upheld, which the driver side will use to argue the rider is a repeat late-canceller.

The GPS record is partly unhelpful to us: the driver was within 200 m from 17:17:50 and stayed within range for 4 min 40 s (F2, F3) — on a plain reading the rider was inside a 200 m radius of a waiting car and did not board, which the driver will use under NS-1(iii).

The driver's chat at 17:19 (F10) and 17:22 (F11) supports his version that he was waiting at the pickup and had waited over 3 minutes; the timeline's null arrival tap (F7) conflicts with the driver statement (F12) and is our case's narrowest point.
The driver's clean record (F17: 394 trips in 90 d, rating 4.4, 0 disputes) makes a fraud-style flag_account referral harder to sustain, and flag_account can only ever be an add-on, not the outcome.

claims.assertion: The GPS record shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup point from 17:17:50 and remained there for 4 min 40 s in total before cancellation, so the driver was physically at the pick-up location as required by NS-1 (ii).

The driver waited well beyond the 3-minute threshold: cumulative time inside 200 m before cancellation was 4 min 40 s and the driver sat stationary from 17:18:25 to 17:22:30 (4 min 5 s) just 53 m from the pickup, satisfying the waiting requirement of NS-1 (iii).

The driver indicated arrival: platform receipt and chat both place an arrival indication at the pickup, with the driver messaging "I'm here at the pickup point" at 17:19 while 38–53 m away, so the requirement in NS-1 (i) is met on the system record.

The driver cancelled only after the waiting period elapsed — the cancellation was at 17:22:30, 4 min 40 s after the recorded arrival at 17:17:50, confirming the cancellation followed the completed wait required by NS-1 rather than preceding it.

The $6.61 cancellation fee on record is exactly the published rider cancellation fee, with no surge applied (1.0×) and no additional unpublished charge added, so the amount charged is the correct one for a valid no-show cancellation under NS-0/NS-1.

The driver's account history shows 394 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes in 90 days and 0 upheld, which supports that this is an isolated, properly conducted no-show cancellation rather than a pattern of fee abuse — no NS-2 account flag is warranted on this record.

The rider's own profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in the last 90 days out of 3 disputes, which is consistent with a repeated pattern of not appearing at the pickup point rather than a one-off driver error.

weaknesses: The 'I'm Here' button record is internally inconsistent in the fact table: F6 says the driver tapped it at 17:18:50, 38 m from pickup, while F7 (timeline) states driver_pressed_here_at is null (never tapped). The rider will rely on F7 to argue NS-1 (i) fails, which would trigger the full refund under NS-2.

The rider will cite F5/F4 that the driver sat stationary (F3) 53 m from the pickup and never made closer contact, arguing the driver left too early and that a 34 m closest approach (F1) plus no further contact does not prove a genuine no-show; the rider's message-based account that they arrived 'a minute later' is not corroborated by any system record, but the arrival-proximity argument still bites.

If the judge resolves the F6/F7 conflict against the driver, NS-2 would require not only a full refund of $6.61 but also a flag_account on the driver for pressing 'I'm Here' while (on F7's reading) no valid tap exists — an adverse outcome for my client.

points.response: I accept the GPS half of D1 (F2: within 200 m from 17:17:50, 4 min 40 s cumulative), but NS-1 requires (i) AND (ii) AND (iii) together, and (i) fails because the timeline shows no arrival tap at all (F7).

Conceded as to duration: the driver was stationary 4 min 5 s inside the radius (F3), longer than 3 minutes, so NS-1(iii) is met — but those minutes only count toward the fee if the arrival indication in NS-1(i) exists, and F7 shows it does not.

D3 substitutes a chat message for the required app action: NS-1(i) requires that the driver pressed "I'm Here", and the timeline value for that tap is null (F7); a text message at 17:19 (F10) cannot cure the missing button press, and F6's reading of a tap is contradicted by that same timeline record.

D4 conflates the platform's recorded "arrival" (F5) with the driver's required arrival indication; the system record shows the arrival button was never tapped (F7), so the 4 min 40 s elapsed does not complete the NS-1 sequence and NS-0 sends the fee to NS-2.

D5 proves only that the amount matches the published figure (F8, F9); the fee still requires the NS-1 conditions to hold, and since (i) fails (F7) the charge is unauthorised under NS-2 whatever the correct dollar amount is.

D6 argues against an aggravating weight rather than defending the fee: the driver's clean history (F17) does not establish NS-1(i), and the flag_account consequence under NS-2 follows from the missing "I'm Here" record (F7), not from the account's trip count.

Profile data may never decide a case: F16's two previously upheld no-show disputes cannot replace the system record here, and in this very instance the record they need — a valid arrival tap — is absent (F7).

I do not withdraw C3; I sharpen it: the driver's written claim that he "pressed I'm Here" (F12) is contradicted by the null timeline field (F7), and the system record prevails over that statement and over his chat messages (F10, F11).
Conceded only as to the framing: the $6.61 fee (F4, F8) does stand or fall on NS-1, and on the system record every element of NS-1 is satisfied, so the charge is valid.

NS-1(i) is met on the same system record they rely on: F6 states the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:18:50, 38 m from the pickup, and stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap; F7's null field is a single inconsistent timeline entry, not the only arrival evidence.

The system record is not uniform: F6 (timeline, system source) positively records the tap at 17:18:50 with the exact distance, while F7 merely records a null field, so the driver's statement (F12) and chat (F10) are corroborated by system data rather than contradicted by it.

NS-2 only triggers if NS-1 (i), (ii) or (iii) fails; here (ii) holds — the driver was inside 200 m from 17:17:50 for a cumulative 4 min 40 s (F2, F3) — and (iii) holds with over 4 minutes of waiting, so no full refund under NS-2 is owed.

The same timeline they cite (F5, F6) records both a platform-recorded arrival at 17:17:50 and the "I'm Here" tap at 17:18:50, and F3 shows the driver stationary only 53 m away until 17:22:30; a driver who is present, stationary and waiting for 4 min 40 s has not committed the evidential gap NS-2 addresses.

The rider's account is a statement with no system support: the GPS record shows the closest approach was 34 m at 17:18:20 and the driver sat 53 m away for 4 min 5 s (F1, F3), so nothing in the system record shows the rider reaching the car within the wait; the rider's own profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F16).

Traffic and weather facts are irrelevant to NS-1, which turns only on the arrival tap, GPS proximity and the 3-minute wait; F13–F15 neither add nor remove any NS-1 condition, and F2/F3 already establish the wait.

NS-2's flag_account applies only where the GPS shows the driver was not at the pickup when the button was pressed; here the driver was 38 m away at the tap (F6) and within 200 m throughout (F2), and his clean record of 394 trips with 0 disputes (F17) gives no basis for a fraud referral.
